summary: 60-foot Aermotor tower on Bear Mountain, Fresno County, California, with a CCC residence; now a restricted communications site behind a locked gate, registered 2019.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot observation cab; CCC residence built to Forest Service BC-201 plan
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Cal Fire Fresno-Kings Unit

access.note: Register says the lookout is not readily accessible to the public: over 4 miles behind a locked gate on a paved road

visit.drive_up: Paved road to the station, past a locked gate more than 4 miles back

events.note: Residents of three fire districts petitioned the county for a lookout station; volunteer crews worked on the station and telephone lines in May
Station reported blown down in July 1925
State announced construction of a 60-foot steel tower in March 1927; Register dates the tower to circa 1927
Agreement with Fresno County announced October 1927; the state to maintain a summer lookout on the mountain
Lightning struck the lookout, knocking out telephone lines and the station's radio transmitter
Historic garage removed and destroyed; Register says the garage and residence cabin had been removed by 2007

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives an early-1900s tower date. The 1923 newspaper items describe a new station being set up, and the 1927 item and Register point to about 1927. The story uses the 1920s dates and notes the Wikipedia conflict.
Register says the garage and residence cabin were removed by 2007; the 2007 report names only the garage. The story attributes the house removal to the Register alone.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 18.3 matches 60 feet (NHLR). Brief built 1927 is stated as circa 1927 in NHLR; no correction proposed. Elevation 1,035 m (NHLR) matches the brief. Access moved from unknown to restricted per NHLR (undated quote from a 1991 visit, MVT 10/91, and the 2019 register text). No source read gives current staffing, current fire-detection use, or a 2020s visit. A June 2024 lightning fire that damaged transmitters on Bear Mountain appears in search results (KMPH, Fresno Bee, Newscast Studio) but the Fresno Bee page timed out and was not read, so it is left out; worth checking. Forest Lookouts and the 2007 report disagree on the house's fate only through the Register. The area is 'Squaw Valley' in these sources; a later name change was seen only in an unreliable mirror and was not verified. No photos added; the Register's 1955 Cal Fire photos have no image URLs in the text read.
